name: Revoker — Approval Sentinel
description: Watches Approval events on the agent's own wallet, filters for unlimited grants, and escalates to the Revoker agent's POST /revoke callback — which performs the atomic check-and-execute revoke. Detection and alerting live in the workflow; the write stays server-side and atomic. Placeholders ${REVOKER_CALLBACK_URL}, ${REVOKER_CALLBACK_SECRET}, ${REVOKER_WATCHED_TOKEN} and ${REVOKER_WATCHED_WALLET} are substituted from the environment by scripts/deploy-workflow.ts; no secret is committed.

data.label: Approval
data.description: Fires on every ERC-20 Approval event emitted by the watched token. The ABI is supplied explicitly because the demo token is an unverified throwaway deploy, so KeeperHub cannot auto-fetch it.

data.label: Unlimited, and ours
data.description: Two tests, both of which must hold. The allowance test is exact equality with type(uint256).max, mirroring the agent's own `unlimited-to-unverified` rule rather than inventing a looser threshold for the workflow. The owner test exists because the trigger sees every Approval on the token, and only the agent's own wallet is revocable — KeeperHub signs for that account and no other.

data.label: Revoke via agent
data.description: The seam. This does NOT write to the chain — it asks the Revoker agent to, and the agent performs the revoke as a single server-side check-and-execute. That is why the workflow round-trip cannot re-open the TOCTOU race: the allowance re-read and the approve(spender,0) still happen inside one KeeperHub operation, and this call happens strictly before it. failOnError is off because a landing that needs the fee-escalation ladder can outlast the 30s HTTP ceiling; a timeout must escalate to a human, not silently end the run.

data.label: Confirmed on chain?
data.description: The agent reports four dispositions and only one of them means the allowance is gone. Branching on it is what keeps this workflow from posting a success alert for a transaction that reverted or never landed.

data.label: Alert — revoked
data.description: Carries the explorer link the agent read back off the execution record, so the alert links to evidence rather than asserting success.

data.label: Alert — needs a human
data.description: Everything that is not a confirmed revoke: reverted, still pending past the agent's 75s budget, skipped because the allowance was already zero, an HTTP timeout, or an outright refusal. Deliberately one loud branch rather than silence — a sentinel whose failures are quieter than its wins is not a sentinel.
